notes: Saved at Q4 publish. Re-save from src/content/experiences before the Q1 2027 update if data changes mid-quarter.

asakusa-kimono-matcha-sweets.name: Asakusa Kimono Tea Ceremony with Matcha and Sweets
asakusa-kimono-matcha-sweets.editor_note: Kimono dressing, matcha and wagashi in a single Asakusa booking: the easy pick if the photos matter as much as the tea. Platform-only listing we haven't visited ourselves.
asakusa-kimono-matcha-sweets.price_note: from ¥8,400 per person, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

casual-tea-asakusa.name: Casual Tea Ceremony (Tokyo Tourist Lounge Asakusa)
casual-tea-asakusa.editor_note: A relaxed, photos-welcome session — honest about being casual rather than formal. Platform-only operator with strong reviews; we haven't visited ourselves.
casual-tea-asakusa.price_note: ¥4,500 per person, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

chazen-asakusa.name: Chazen Asakusa
chazen-asakusa.editor_note: A properly built tea room, complete with tsukubai water basin and nijiriguchi crawl-through entrance — rare among tourist venues. Handles larger groups well.
chazen-asakusa.price_note: ¥3,500 shared / ¥4,500 private session. Source: third-party articles, July 2026.

chazen-ginza.name: Chazen Ginza (main branch)
chazen-ginza.editor_note: A properly built tea room with tsukubai and nijiriguchi, next door to the Kabuki-za theatre — easy to make a full day of traditional culture.
chazen-ginza.price_note: from ¥3,500 shared / from ¥5,000 private session, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

hamarikyu-nakajima.name: Hamarikyu Gardens — Nakajima-no-Ochaya
hamarikyu-nakajima.editor_note: This is a café, not a ceremony — which makes it perfect if a full tea ceremony feels like more commitment than you want.
hamarikyu-nakajima.notes: Matcha and wagashi in a garden teahouse; entry-level 'tea moment' rather than a ceremony.
hamarikyu-nakajima.price_note: from ¥1,000, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03. Garden entry fee charged separately.

happoen-shirokanedai.name: Happo-en Garden Tea Ceremony
happoen-shirokanedai.editor_note: A genuinely beautiful garden venue, and the experience can be custom-designed to your group on request.

hisui-tokyo-ginza.name: HiSUi TOKYO (Ginza)
hisui-tokyo-ginza.editor_note: A multi-discipline cultural school; hosts take time to explain the seasonal meaning behind each utensil and the spirit of hospitality.
hisui-tokyo-ginza.price_note: Tea ceremony plan from ¥13,200 per person, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

imperial-hotel-tokoan.name: Imperial Hotel Tokyo — Toko-an Tea Room (Hibiya)
imperial-hotel-tokoan.editor_note: A tea room inside the Imperial Hotel, bookable online. The base plan is tea and sweets in about 30 minutes; pick the longer plan if you want to whisk a bowl yourself.
imperial-hotel-tokoan.price_note: ¥5,000 tea and sweets (about 30 min) / ¥8,000 with matcha-making (about 60 min), tax and service included, from the official page, read 2026-11-03.
imperial-hotel-tokoan.notes: 4F Main Building. Tatami seating. 10:00-16:00, closed Sundays and public holidays. Sometimes fully booked for private functions.

jidaiya-asakusa.name: Asakusa Jidaiya Tea Ceremony
jidaiya-asakusa.editor_note: Kimono and tea with chairs available, but the space is a studio rather than a tea room — enjoyable, though firmly an 'experience' rather than the real setting.
jidaiya-asakusa.price_note: Solo travelers pay ¥11,000; ¥5,500 pp for two or more, tax incl.

jugetsudo-ginza.name: Jugetsudo Tea Ceremony (Kabukiza Tower)
jugetsudo-ginza.editor_note: A very light, simplified matcha tasting rather than anything close to a ceremony.
jugetsudo-ginza.notes: Kengo Kuma-designed cafe; matcha starter set included as gift
jugetsudo-ginza.price_note: from ¥3,600 per person, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

koboji-temple-private.name: Private Tea Ceremony at Kobohji Temple (Mita)
koboji-temple-private.editor_note: The rare option to wear an Oshima Tsumugi silk haori is a lovely touch. Who actually performs the ceremony is unclear — not yet verified first-hand.
koboji-temple-private.price_note: ¥20,000 per person, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.
koboji-temple-private.notes: Venue correction by editor: temple is likely Kobohji (弘法寺) in Mita, not Asakusa. Verify address before publishing.

maikoya-asakusa.name: Maikoya Asakusa — Kimono Tea Ceremony
maikoya-asakusa.editor_note: Kimono dressing, private bookings, even nerikiri sweet-making add-ons — the pick if you want a broad cultural bundle rather than tea alone.
maikoya-asakusa.price_note: from ¥7,700 per person, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

maikoya-shinjuku.name: Maikoya Shinjuku — Kimono Tea Ceremony
maikoya-shinjuku.editor_note: Same broad bundle as the Asakusa branch — kimono, private options, sweet-making — with the bonus of being walkable from Shinjuku Station.
maikoya-shinjuku.price_note: from ¥4,400 per person, tea ceremony only (kimono not included), confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

matcha-kimono-tea-shinjuku.name: Matcha Kimono Tea Ceremony (Shinjuku)
matcha-kimono-tea-shinjuku.editor_note: Easy access from Shinjuku, with matcha and wagashi in a relaxed session. Tables and cushions rather than tatami make it comfortable for visitors unused to floor seating.
matcha-kimono-tea-shinjuku.price_note: from ¥9,500 per person, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

minamikaze-sumida.name: Teahouse Minamikaze (Sumida)
minamikaze-sumida.editor_note: Chairs rather than tatami, and you whisk your own bowl after watching the host prepare the first — an easy, hands-on session for visitors. But skip the tatami room and this won't give you the atmosphere of a real tea room or its utensils.
minamikaze-sumida.notes: 292 Viator reviews, 'Top 1%' badge. Two-bowl format: guest first drinks tea prepared by host, then prepares their own. 6th-floor building near Asakusa/Skytree, not a dedicated teahouse.
minamikaze-sumida.price_note: ¥9,800 per person, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

ocharu-nezu.name: Ocharu Tea Experience (near The University of Tokyo / Nezu)
ocharu-nezu.editor_note: A multi-tea tasting (black tea, gyokuro) rather than a tea ceremony. If matcha ritual is what you came for, look elsewhere — as a tea tasting it may suit you fine.
ocharu-nezu.notes: Modern multi-tea tasting (wakocha, gyokuro) rather than a formal ceremony.
ocharu-nezu.price_note: ¥6,000 per person, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

senrakuan-sendagi.name: Senraku-an Small Tea Room (Sendagi)
senrakuan-sendagi.editor_note: A small tea room in Sendagi, a quiet old-Tokyo neighborhood next to Yanaka, far calmer than the Asakusa crowds. Platform-only listing we haven't visited ourselves.
senrakuan-sendagi.price_note: from ¥8,000 per person per a GetYourGuide-powered listing (jasumo.com), read 2026-11-03. Not yet confirmed on GetYourGuide itself.
senrakuan-sendagi.notes: 4-18-19 Sendagi, Bunkyo. About 7 min walk from Nishi-Nippori Station.

shizu-kokoro-asakusa.name: Shizu-Kokoro Tea Ceremony School
shizu-kokoro-asakusa.editor_note: The instructor has taught in the US and runs an actual tea school; this is the closest a visitor gets to a real keiko practice lesson.
shizu-kokoro-asakusa.notes: Koicha and usucha both served; guest and host roles; monthly seasonal themes. Priority for a first-hand review visit.
shizu-kokoro-asakusa.price_note: from ¥5,500 per person, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

tea-room-kakoi-shibuya.name: Tea Room Kakoi (Shibuya)
tea-room-kakoi-shibuya.editor_note: Organic matcha tasting angle is appealing, but this is a platform-only operator we haven't verified first-hand.
tea-room-kakoi-shibuya.price_note: ¥7,500 per person, confirmed by Ayaka on the booking page, 2026-11-03.

tokyo-chaan-shibuya.name: Tokyo Chaan (Shibuya)
tokyo-chaan-shibuya.editor_note: Small English-led sessions a five-minute walk from Shibuya Station, with the host in kimono. An easy first ceremony; there's no kimono rental, so come as you are.
tokyo-chaan-shibuya.price_note: ¥3,900 shared / ¥7,800 private per adult, from the official plans page, read 2026-11-03.
tokyo-chaan-shibuya.notes: 2F Manji Building, 1-15-9 Dogenzaka. 45-60 minutes. Free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

urasenke-youwakai.name: Urasenke YOUWAKAI Tea Ceremony
urasenke-youwakai.editor_note: Well-known tea practitioners are involved in this school, and the tea room is unusually spacious. It takes a little courage to inquire, but this opens the door to the real depth of the culture.
urasenke-youwakai.notes: Usucha (thin tea) program. Hosted with involvement of Sosei Ajioka. Reservations accepted Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays only. Same school as author — priority for first-hand review visit.

wasako-asakusa.name: Wasako Japanese-Style Room (Asakusa)
wasako-asakusa.editor_note: Sixty minutes in a Japanese-style room steps from Asakusa Station, with a choice of tatami or chairs. Platform-only operator we haven't verified first-hand.
wasako-asakusa.price_note: from ¥7,000 per person per a GetYourGuide-powered listing (jasumo.com), read 2026-11-03. Not yet confirmed on GetYourGuide itself.
wasako-asakusa.notes: 5F Collection Kaminarimon Building, 2-18-15 Kaminarimon. Near Asakusa Station Exit A4.
